title: Private control plane — onboarding & ops cheat sheet (VPC / on-prem)
content:
Purpose
This is a pragmatic, lightweight cheat-sheet for engineers and SREs onboarding a Redwood private control plane into a customer VPC or on-prem environment. Focus: initial provisioning, Terraform module notes, horizontal scale steps, and certificate/instance rotations. Not exhaustive — use alongside the formal runbooks and customer-specific network diagrams.

Scope
- Applies to Private Control Plane (control-plane services + Postgres + object storage connectors) deployed to customer VPCs or on-prem racks using our Terraform modules and installation artifacts.
- Assumes customer has: network diagram, a reachable bastion for ops, KMS/HSM access (optional), and approved CIDR/IP allowlists.

Quick inventory (what to gather before starting)
- AWS account / VPC IDs or on-prem network VLANs.
- Public IPs / NAT / egress rules for telemetry and package download.
- Certificate signing authority (internal CA or customer-managed).
- KMS/HSM creds (if using envelope encryption for secrets).
- Static IP or load balancer for control plane API endpoints.
- Postgres credentials and S3-compatible bucket details (or MinIO endpoint).
- Terraform state backend (s3/consul/enterprise) access and locking config.
- Contact list: customer network lead, security, and on-call SRE.

Network & security checklist
- Confirm outbound egress to: updates.redwood.ai (443), metrics.redwood.ai (443), container registry endpoints.
- Ensure internal DNS resolves control-plane hostnames; split-horizon DNS recommended for private IP resolution.
- Security groups / firewalls: control-plane nodes allow inbound from customer-app subnets on API ports + SSH from bastion only.
- Database access: only allow Postgres port from control-plane subnet.
- KMS/HSM: test a sample encrypt/decrypt with customer creds before provisioning.

Terraform module notes (practical pointers)
- Modules used: rp-controlplane-core, rp-controlplane-iam, rp-controlplane-db, rp-networking. Keep module versions pinned in terraform.tfvars to avoid surprise changes.
- State: always enable remote state locking (DynamoDB for AWS) and point to the customer-approved state bucket.
- Variables we commonly override: instance_type, desired_replicas, disk_size_gb, database_instance_class, disable_public_subnets (true for VPC-only installs).
- Outputs to capture post-apply: control_plane_lb_dns, control_plane_api_cert_fingerprint, db_endpoint, rmq_endpoint (if used).
- Common gotchas: forgetting to set kms_key_arn for secret encryption (defaults to empty and will store plaintext in state outputs).

Sample terraform snippet (for ops reference)
- In terraform.tfvars: 
  control_plane_version = "2024-08-patch1"
  instance_type = "m6i.large"
  desired_replicas = 3
  kms_key_arn = "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01"

Applying safely
- Workflow: terraform plan -> peer review -> terraform apply from CI agent with ephemeral creds or via a locked bastion.
- Apply windows: schedule during customer maintenance window; for on-prem target nights/weekends.
- Preflight checklist (quick): terraform plan contains only expected changes; no accidental DB replacement; KMS key present; load balancer config checked.

Rolling upgrade steps (control plane version change)
1) Create a canary subset: set desired_replicas_canary = 1 and tag instance group canary.
2) Apply terraform to provision canary instances with new control_plane_version.
3) Health checks: wait for canary to pass 10m of traffic-injected smoke tests (see smoke tests below).
4) If canary good -> increase desired_replicas by 1 per 5–10 minutes across instance groups to avoid database connection spikes.
5) Monitor: error rate, API latency 95p, DB connections, memory. Keep rollback step ready (set desired_replicas back to previous AMI/version or change version var).

Scale-up / scale-down (horizontal)
- Scale-up: edit terraform var desired_replicas or use autoscaling hooks if available. For large jumps (>2x), scale in steps and monitor DB connection pool and redis/KV cache saturation.
- Scale-down: cordon instance in orchestration layer (k8s: kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets) then drop desired_replicas and terraform apply. Wait for graceful shutdown and KV cache warm-up on survivors.

Rotation procedures
- TLS cert rotation (external customer CA):
  1) Upload new cert to secrets store (encrypt with KMS).
  2) Update terraform var control_plane_tls_cert_ref -> apply to add new cert as non-primary.
  3) Wait 5 minutes; flip primary certificate pointer to new cert in runtime config via admin API.
  4) Restart API pods on one AZ at a time: kubectl rollout restart deployment/control-plane-api -n redwood --selector=zone=azX.
  5) Verify TLS chain and SNI on LB.
- KMS key rotation: coordinate with customer and update kms_key_arn in terraform, run terraform apply which will trigger secrets rewrap job. Monitor for failed decrypts in logs.
- Node replacement (compromised or degraded):
  1) Mark node out of LB and orchestration: kubectl cordon <node>; remove from LB target group.
  2) Terraform taint the instance resource (or remove instance and let ASG replace).
  3) Apply changes and wait for new node to join; run health probes and synthetic smoke tests.

Database migrations and backups
- We use managed Postgres where possible; ensure RPO/RTO meet customer SLA before major upgrades.
- Before schema migrations: take logical backup (pg_dump) and snapshot. Store snapshot id in ticket.
- Use zero-downtime migration patterns where possible (backfill columns, update app side to write/read dual columns).
- Rollback: restore from snapshot to a staging DB and validate; production rollback requires approval from product & customer.

Smoke tests (quick list to run after any change)
- API: GET /health -> 200 and JSON {status:ok}.
- Auth: issue token via oidc flow and access protected route.
- Model load: load a small model and run a 10-token generation request, assert latency < target.
- DB: simple read/write to config table.
- Metrics: pipeline emits metrics to our metrics endpoint for the new nodes.

Observability & SLO checks
- Dashboards to watch: control-plane-latency (p50/p95/p99), control-plane-errors, db-connections, kube-pod-restarts.
- Alerting: create temporary high-severity alerts during major ops (pager duty to on-call + escalation to platform lead).

Rollback checklist (fast)
- If API errors spike >5% or DB connections > 90% of max after a change:
  1) Revert terraform var control_plane_version to previous value and apply immediately.
  2) If revert does not heal within 15 minutes, scale down new instances and scale up old ones (use snapshots/AMI IDs pinned in terraform).
  3) Restore DB from snapshot only if schema corruption detected.

Communication & approvals
- Before: approvals from customer security and network.
- During: post progress to deployment Slack channel (ops-private-controlplane) every 15 minutes during the window.
- After: deliver a short postmortem if anything significant happened; include metrics, timeline, and rollback points.

Example run checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Confirm maintenance window and runbook owner.
- [ ] Validate terraform plan against expected changes.
- [ ] Snapshot DB and store snapshot id in ticket.
- [ ] Apply canary changes.
- [ ] Run smoke tests and verify metrics.
- [ ] Progressive rollout to full fleet.
- [ ] Final validation and close ticket.

Notes & TODOs (ideas for next doc iteration)
- Add prescriptive Terraform CI job examples (locking, drift detection, automated rollback on failed health checks).
- Expand sample smoke-test harness and include scripts for synthetic traffic.
- Add checklist for fully air-gapped installs where outbound connectivity is forbidden.
- Document recommended instance types and disk IOPS recommendations per scale tier.

Contact / escalation
- Primary: Sasha Nguyen (eng-private-deployments) — sasha@redwood.ai
- Secondary: Marcus Li (platform eng) — marcus@redwood.ai
- Security contact: Priya Chandrasekar — priya@redwood.ai

End of cheat-sheet — treat as operational shorthand. Save canonical runbook updates back to Confluence and link here when final.
